extracted.intended_audience: NIH/NIAID U01 applicants and peer reviewers (PD/PIs, institutional grants offices, review panel members)
extracted.subtask_description: Summary statement and review criteria used by an NIAID Special Emphasis Panel to evaluate a U01 grant application (Significance, Investigators, Innovation, Approach, Environment) including human/animal protections, resource sharing, and budget recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem? Will the study increase knowledge or have an impact on the field (e.g., predicting antibody-mediated effector functions of antibody combinations; mapping IgG isotypes across species)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers list strengths (e.g., potential to enable prediction of antibody effectiveness, extension of models to mixed IgG compositions) and weaknesses (e.g., lack of preliminary data demonstrating synergistic/antagonistic pairs, unclear translational relevance). Consider whether the proposed work will likely increase knowledge and its likely impact; note if key hypotheses lack supporting preliminary data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD/PI(s) and team well qualified to conduct the work? Is the multiple PD/PI leadership plan adequate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess track records, complementary expertise, collaborations, and leadership plans. Strengths cited include strong publication records and recognized expertise; weaknesses noted when absent (none were noted for this application). Evaluate adequacy of MPI leadership plan and potential for collaborative execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project challenge current paradigms or develop novel concepts, models, or methods (e.g., multivalent binding model for mixed IgG compositions; homology map for cross-species IgG function)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify novel aspects vs refinements of existing work. Strengths: new models or integration of modeling/experiment. Weaknesses: if methods are minor refinements or unlikely to reveal new insights, or if identified discoveries may have limited practical utility (e.g., therapies favoring single active molecules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methods, analyses, and potential problems/alternatives appropriate and well-reasoned for achieving the aims (e.g., modeling + in vitro/in vivo validation; feasibility of measuring multivalent binding)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review method feasibility, controls, measurement limits, assumptions, alternative strategies, and how limitations are addressed. Specific anti-patterns: ignoring receptor reorganization, excluding other cell-cell interface ligands (ICAM-1/LFA-1), assuming uniform affinity despite heterogeneous glycosylation, failing to consider measuring very tight binding (picomolar KDs). Consider whether data generation methods may reduce model rigor (heterogeneous immune complexes, kinetic lability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment, institutional support, and resources contribute to success of the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess institutional facilities, collaborative environment, and suitability for proposed computational and experimental tasks. Strengths: exceptional environments at host institutions; weaknesses noted when environment is inadequate (none noted here).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact / Priority Score
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewers' assessment of the likelihood that the project will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the field; committee assigns an Overall Impact (1-9) which is averaged and multiplied by 10 for the Impact/Priority score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting but are not specifically discussed or calculated into the overall impact score. The Overall Impact reflects committee discussion; scoring method: average overall scores given by voting reviewers (1-9) then multiply by 10. Percentiles may also be assigned for some applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans to protect human subjects and determination of applicability (e.g., 'Not applicable (CODE 10)' if no human subjects involved).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When human subjects are involved, reviewers evaluate protections and may rate applicability. If not applicable, indicate code 10. Ensure human subjects sections are adequate when applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animal Protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of vertebrate animal welfare and adequacy of the animal care and use description (e.g., 'ACCEPTABLE (CODE 30)').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate whether protection of vertebrate animals is adequately described and identify any concerns. Provide sufficient detail on animal models and welfare practices to receive an acceptable determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans to prevent risks when handling biohazard materials or samples (e.g., 'ACCEPTABLE').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide adequate biosafety plans and protocols. Lack of adequate biohazard protection is a weakness; acceptable plans should describe containment and risk mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion Plans (Women, Minorities, Across Lifespan)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plans for inclusion of women, minorities, and individuals across the lifespan; may be noted as not applicable when human subjects are not involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, inclusion plans must be appropriate and specific. If not applicable, indicate accordingly. Reviewers will note applicability and adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans (Data/Model Organism/Genomic Data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of data sharing and resource sharing plans (e.g., Data Sharing Plans: 'ACCEPTABLE'; Model Organism Sharing: 'NOT APPLICABLE'; Genomic Data: 'NOT APPLICABLE').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear plans for data sharing; acceptable plans are noted. If not applicable, state so. Adequate data sharing plans are considered a positive item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of plans to authenticate key biological and/or chemical resources (e.g., cell lines, antibodies), noted as 'ACCEPTABLE' when adequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe procedures for validation/authentication of critical reagents. Adequate plans mitigate risks from misidentified or contaminated resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgetary Overlap and Committee Budget Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers and staff check for budgetary overlap; committee makes budget recommendations but the award budget will be calculated by institute grants management staff based on recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare any budgetary overlap. Note that the administrative requested budget may be adjusted; committee can recommend budgets 'as requested' or with modification. If award planned, grants management will finalize costs per recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translational Relevance / Cross‑Species Mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of how well findings in model systems (e.g., mice, humanized mice) will translate to human biology and the adequacy of plans to map murine and human IgG isotypes/functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate assumptions linking species (homology maps) and adequacy of experimental designs to distinguish murine vs human contributions in humanized models. Weaknesses include unclear translatability, untested assumptions of conservation, or inability to distinguish human vs murine components in humanized models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary Data and Identification of Key Phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether there are sufficient preliminary results demonstrating key phenomena the proposal intends to study (e.g., evidence of synergistic or antagonistic IgG pairs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of preliminary data supporting the existence or detectability of predicted effects is a significant weakness. Reviewers expect illustrative preliminary results or rationale that justifies the proposed aims and methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling Methods Adequacy and Alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the modeling approaches, whether they are novel vs refinements, and whether alternative methods/contingencies are considered if current tools prove inadequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether modeling schemas are up-to-date, scalable to multivariate complexity, and whether investigators considered alternatives. Anti-patterns: relying solely on older/limited tools without contingency plans; failing to add parameters or consider alternative analytical approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental Measurement Feasibility (Sensitivity/Accuracy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of feasibility and rigor of proposed measurements (e.g., measuring tight binding in the picomolar range, reagent heterogeneity affecting affinity measurements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether methods can accurately measure very low KDs, whether incubation times/equilibrium assumptions hold, and whether reagent heterogeneity (TNP-BSA valency, glycosylation variability, Fab engagement) introduces unacceptable variance. If measurements are likely made far from equilibrium, models may be skewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of Cell‑Cell Interface Complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the proposed models/experiments account for biological complexity at the immune synapse (e.g., receptor reorganization, other ligands like ICAM-1/LFA-1 affecting ADCC/ADCP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models focusing exclusively on Fc-FcR interactions should justify omission of other interface components; failure to consider receptor reorganization or additional ligands is flagged as a weakness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical Analysis Appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of chosen statistical methods (e.g., use of Pearson correlation vs non-parametric methods when distributions are non-normal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose statistical tests appropriate for data distributions (e.g., Spearman for non-normal data). Reviewers note minor methodological weaknesses when parametric tests are used inappropriately.
